meta.name: The Field and the Knower of the Field
meta.outline: Verses 1–6: the body is the field, and the one who knows it is the knower of the field; 7–11: twenty qualities that together are called knowledge; 12–18: Brahman, the thing to be known; 19–23: nature and the spirit; 24–26: different ways of seeing the Self; 27–34: the one Lord, the same in all beings, who does not act and is not stained. Some editions begin this chapter with a question from Arjuna and count 35 verses; the numbering here follows the 34-verse count.

verses.speaker: Krishna
skt: एतद्यो वेत्ति तं प्राहुः क्षेत्रज्ञ इति तद्विदः
words: is called the knower of the field
by those who understand these things
verses.tr: Krishna said: This body, Arjuna, is called the field. The one who knows it is called the knower of the field by those who understand these things.

verses.speaker: Krishna
skt: क्षेत्रज्ञं चापि मां विद्धि सर्वक्षेत्रेषु भारत
words: know me also as the knower of the field
knowledge of the field and its knower
that, in my view, is true knowledge
verses.tr: Know me, Arjuna, as the knower of the field in every field. Knowledge of the field and of its knower is, in my view, true knowledge.

verses.speaker: Krishna
skt: तत्क्षेत्रं यच्च यादृक् च यद्विकारि यतश्च यत्
स च यो यत्प्रभावश्च तत्समासेन मे शृणु
words: and who he, the knower, is
hear that from me in brief
verses.tr: Hear from me in brief what the field is, what it is like, how it changes and where it comes from, and also who the knower is and what his powers are.

verses.speaker: Krishna
words: it has been sung by the sages in many ways
and in the words of the Brahma Sutras
which are well reasoned and certain
verses.tr: The sages have sung of this in many ways, in various Vedic hymns, and also in the well-reasoned and certain words of the Brahma Sutras.

verses.speaker: Krishna
words: the ten senses and the one, the mind
and the five objects of the senses
verses.tr: The five great elements, the sense of “I”, the intellect and unseen nature; the ten senses and the mind, and the five objects of the senses;

verses.speaker: Krishna
words: this, in brief, is the field
verses.tr: desire and dislike, pleasure and pain, the body as a whole, consciousness and steadiness: this, in brief, is the field, together with its changes.

verses.speaker: Krishna
verses.tr: Humility, freedom from pretence, non-violence, patience, honesty, service to the teacher, purity, steadiness and self-control;

verses.speaker: Krishna
words: detachment from the objects of the senses
seeing the suffering in birth, death, old age and illness
verses.tr: detachment from the objects of the senses, freedom from ego, and seeing clearly the suffering in birth, death, old age and illness;

verses.speaker: Krishna
words: to children, spouse, home and the rest
and a mind that is always even
when wanted or unwanted things happen
verses.tr: non-attachment, and not clinging to children, spouse, home and the rest; a mind that stays even whether wanted or unwanted things happen;

verses.speaker: Krishna
words: and for me, with undivided yoga
verses.tr: devotion to me that never strays, with undivided yoga; a liking for quiet places and no taste for crowds;

verses.speaker: Krishna
words: constancy in knowledge of the Self
seeing the purpose of knowing the truth
this is declared to be knowledge
and what is other than this is ignorance
verses.tr: constancy in knowledge of the Self, and seeing what knowledge of the truth is for: this is declared to be knowledge. Whatever is otherwise is ignorance.

verses.speaker: Krishna
words: I shall tell you what is to be known
the supreme Brahman, which has no beginning
न सत् तत् न असत् उच्यते
it is said to be neither being nor non-being
verses.tr: I shall tell you what is to be known, knowing which a person reaches immortality. It is the supreme Brahman, which has no beginning. It is said to be neither being nor non-being.

verses.speaker: Krishna
words: it has hands and feet everywhere
it stands, covering everything in the world
verses.tr: It has hands and feet everywhere, eyes, heads and faces everywhere, and ears everywhere. It stands in the world, covering everything.

verses.speaker: Krishna
words: it shines through the working of all the senses
verses.tr: It shines through the working of all the senses, yet it has no senses. It is unattached, yet it supports everything. It is free from the gunas, yet it experiences them.

verses.speaker: Krishna
words: because it is subtle it cannot be grasped
it is far away and also near
verses.tr: It is outside beings and inside them. It does not move, and yet it moves. It is too subtle to be grasped. It is far away, and it is also near.

verses.speaker: Krishna
skt: अविभक्तं च भूतेषु विभक्तमिव च स्थितम्
भूतभर्तृ च तज्ज्ञेयं ग्रसिष्णु प्रभविष्णु च
words: it is to be known as the supporter of beings
which takes them back and brings them forth
verses.tr: It is undivided, yet it seems to be divided among beings. Know it as the supporter of all beings, which takes them back into itself and brings them forth again.

verses.speaker: Krishna
skt: ज्ञानं ज्ञेयं ज्ञानगम्यं हृदि सर्वस्य विष्ठितम्
words: it is the light of all lights
it is knowledge, what is to be known, and what knowledge leads to
it is seated in the heart of everyone
verses.tr: It is the light of all lights, and is said to be beyond darkness. It is knowledge, the thing to be known and the goal of knowledge, and it is seated in the heart of everyone.

verses.speaker: Krishna
skt: इति क्षेत्रं तथा ज्ञानं ज्ञेयं चोक्तं समासतः
words: इति क्षेत्रं तथा ज्ञानं ज्ञेयं च
so the field, knowledge and what is to be known
verses.tr: So the field, knowledge and what is to be known have been described in brief. My devotee who understands this becomes fit to reach my state.

verses.speaker: Krishna
words: know that both have no beginning
and all changes and the gunas
know to be born of nature
verses.tr: Know that nature and the spirit both have no beginning. Know also that all changes and the gunas are born of nature.

verses.speaker: Krishna
words: in producing the body and the senses and their work
nature is said to be the cause
the spirit, in the experiencing of pleasure and pain
is said to be the cause
verses.tr: Nature is said to be the cause behind the body and the senses and what they do. The spirit is said to be the cause behind the experience of pleasure and pain.

verses.speaker: Krishna
words: for the spirit, seated in nature
experiences the gunas born of nature
its attachment to the gunas is the cause
of its births in good and bad wombs
verses.tr: The spirit, seated in nature, experiences the gunas born of nature. Its attachment to the gunas is the cause of its birth in good and bad conditions.

verses.speaker: Krishna
words: and also called the supreme Self
is the supreme spirit in this body
verses.tr: The supreme spirit in this body is called the witness, the one who permits, the supporter, the experiencer, the great Lord and the supreme Self.

verses.speaker: Krishna
skt: य एवं वेत्ति पुरुषं प्रकृतिं च गुणैः सह
words: whoever knows the spirit in this way
and nature along with the gunas
verses.tr: Whoever knows the spirit in this way, and nature with its gunas, is not born again, however that person may be living now.

verses.speaker: Krishna
words: ध्यानेन आत्मनि पश्यन्ति केचित् आत्मानम् आत्मना
some see the Self within themselves by meditation, through the mind
others by the yoga of knowledge (sankhya)
and others by the yoga of action
verses.tr: Some see the Self within themselves through meditation. Others see it through the yoga of knowledge, and others through the yoga of action.

verses.speaker: Krishna
words: but others, who do not know in this way
ते अपि च अतितरन्ति एव मृत्युम्
devoted to what they have heard
verses.tr: Others, who do not know it in these ways, hear of it from others and worship. They too cross beyond death, through their devotion to what they have heard.

verses.speaker: Krishna
words: from the union of the field and its knower
verses.tr: Whatever is born, Arjuna, whether it moves or not, know that it comes from the union of the field and the knower of the field.

verses.speaker: Krishna
words: the supreme Lord living equally in all beings
verses.tr: Whoever sees the supreme Lord living equally in all beings, and not perishing when they perish, truly sees.

verses.speaker: Krishna
skt: न हिनस्त्यात्मनाऽऽत्मानं ततो याति परां गतिम्
words: one does not harm the Self by the self
and so reaches the highest goal
verses.tr: Seeing the same Lord present everywhere, a person does no harm to their own Self, and so reaches the highest goal.

verses.speaker: Krishna
words: प्रकृत्या एव च कर्माणि क्रियमाणानि सर्वशः
that all actions are done by nature alone
and that the Self does nothing
verses.tr: Whoever sees that all actions are done by nature alone, and that the Self does nothing, truly sees.

verses.speaker: Krishna
skt: तत एव च विस्तारं ब्रह्म सम्पद्यते तदा
words: when the many separate states of beings
one sees as resting in the One
and as spreading out from that alone
verses.tr: When a person sees that the many separate forms of beings rest in the One, and spread out from it alone, that person reaches Brahman.

verses.speaker: Krishna
skt: शरीरस्थोऽपि कौन्तेय न करोति न लिप्यते
words: and is free from the gunas
does not act and is not stained
verses.tr: Because it has no beginning and is free from the gunas, Arjuna, this unchanging supreme Self does not act and is not stained, though it lives in the body.

verses.speaker: Krishna
words: is not stained, because it is subtle
so the Self is not stained
verses.tr: As space is everywhere and yet, being subtle, is stained by nothing, so the Self is present everywhere in the body and yet is not stained.

verses.speaker: Krishna
skt: क्षेत्रं क्षेत्री तथा कृत्स्नं प्रकाशयति भारत
words: as the one sun lights up
so the lord of the field lights up the whole field
verses.tr: As the one sun lights up this whole world, Arjuna, so the lord of the field lights up the whole field.

verses.speaker: Krishna
skt: भूतप्रकृतिमोक्षं च ये विदुर्यान्ति ते परम्
words: the difference between the field and its knower
and the freeing of beings from nature
verses.tr: Those who see with the eye of knowledge the difference between the field and its knower, and how beings are set free from nature, reach the supreme.
